title: Rapid endpoint creator: collapse patterns and copy experiments
content:
Purpose and TL;DR:

This note collects experiments for a compact, rapid endpoint creation flow that defaults to safe choices for new users while exposing advanced controls to power users. It also contains multiple microcopy variants for the model version pinning affordance (modal and inline) and sketches for error/fallback messaging. Goal is to settle on a single compact interaction pattern for the MVP and a longer list of backlog experiments (A/B test candidates).

Context and constraints:
- Problem: current create-endpoint flow is long and forces many decisions up-front. Teams want a 30–60s happy-path so devs can test models quickly.
- Requirements: must integrate with model catalog, respect pinned model versions, allow quick rollback to latest compatible variant, and preserve audit metadata for Private/Dedicated customers.
- Safety: default should be: latest verified model variant for the selected model family, autoscale off (single replica), no local overrides to sampling/temperature unless user expands advanced.

Wireframe notes (compact flow):
1) Single-column modal (Rapid Create) – default collapsed advanced panel
  - Top row: Model selector (search + small inline tag showing model family + version chip)
  - Below: Endpoint name (auto-generated placeholder: "my-model-endpoint-1") and small toggle: Public API key enabled (on/off) with short hint text
  - Primary CTA: "Create endpoint" (blue) — creates endpoint with defaults and returns to list with success toast and inline link to console route
  - Secondary: "Create and open" (outline) — creates and opens endpoint details page (for immediate testing)
  - Collapsible accordion: "Advanced settings" (chevron) — reveals target replicas, concurrency, GPU tier, model quantization suggestion, and model pinning toggle
  - Footer: small text: "Need a dedicated pool? See Dedicated plans" which links to product docs

2) Advanced panel (collapsed by default) – progressive disclosure principles
  - Quick suggestions row (one-line) with small CTAs: "Use cost-optimal config" | "Use low-latency config" (both apply a preset inline; user can still fine-tune)
  - Model pinning control: radio buttons "Auto use latest compatible" (default) and "Pin to version" with dropdown of recent versions and a small icon explaining rollback behavior
  - Rollback policy selector: (dropdown) Manual | Canary (10%) | Auto-fallback (to lighter variant on failure)
  - Save as template checkbox (small)

Microcopy experiments: model pinning (inline and modal)
- Variant A (explicit-action first):
  - Inline label: Pin model version
  - Helper: "Pin this endpoint to a specific model version so predictions are stable. Choose 'Auto' to always use the latest verified build."
  - CTA when pinned: "Pinned to v2025-01-15 • Change"

- Variant B (risk-focused):
  - Inline label: Stable outputs (pin version)
  - Helper: "Pinning prevents unexpected output regressions after model updates. Good for critical pipelines."
  - Tooltip copy on hover: "Pins increase reproducibility, but may miss bugfixes — use canary for gradual rollouts."

- Variant C (business-focused):
  - Inline label: SLA-backed version pin
  - Helper: "Enterprise only: lock version and enable SLA monitoring."
  - Small badge if private/dedicated customer: "SLA available"

Confirmation modal copy (when user pins during create):
- Title options: "Lock endpoint to model version?" | "Confirm pin to v2025-01-15"
- Body candidate 1: "Pinning ensures this endpoint will always use version v2025-01-15 of Model-X. You can unpin later or create a canary roll-out to test newer versions."
- Body candidate 2 (short): "This will lock the endpoint to the selected model version. Production traffic will remain unchanged after future model upgrades unless you change this setting."
- Primary CTA: "Confirm and create" (danger/solid)
- Secondary: "Create without pinning"

Error and fallback messaging (examples for inline toast and endpoint details):
- When pinned version is missing in a region: "Pinned version not available in selected region. Endpoint created in fallback mode using latest compatible variant. See details."
- When pin conflicts with hardware: "Selected version requires GPU type A; your plan only supports GPU type B. Choose a different version or upgrade capacity."
- Rollback toast after failed deploy: "Traffic automatically failed over to fallback model (v2024-12-07). We rolled back to keep latency/SLOs. Check audit logs for details."

Accessibility notes:
- All radio/button groups must have aria-labels and short accessible descriptions for screen readers explaining what pinning changes do
- Keyboard flow: collapse/expand should be reachable via Enter and Space; focus should move to the first control inside expanded panel

Backlog grooming (prioritized list)
P0 (MVP):
  - Implement single-column rapid-create modal with collapsed advanced panel (deliverable: prototype + usability test)
  - Default model selection heuristics: latest verified variant; show version chip
  - Pin to version toggle with confirmation modal text variant B (short)

P1:
  - Add quick presets (cost-optimal, low-latency) and wire their telemetry events
  - Add canary rollout option and telemetry to record canary success/failure
  - Audit log entry template for pinned/unpinned actions (for Private customers)

P2:
  - A/B test microcopy variants A and B for pinning helper text across new user cohorts
  - Add per-route per-model token cost estimate in advanced panel
  - Add inline suggestions for quantization (e.g., 4-bit) with expected cost delta

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should "Pin to version" be default for enterprise customers? (Pros: reproducibility; Cons: more support tickets when customers expect automatic fixes)
- Languages: microcopy needs quick localization pass — which strings should be prioritized? (Confirmation modal, inline helper, and toast failures)
- Should rollback/fallback messaging be opt-in for private deployments to avoid automatic fail-overs?

Prototype test plan (quick usability check):
- Recruit 6 internal engineers (3 infra/platform, 3 app devs)
- Tasks: create an endpoint for a test app in < 90s; pin version; open advanced panel and set canary; simulate pinned-version unavailable and observe toast messaging
- Success metrics: median task time < 90s, task completion 90%+, 0 critical accessibility failures

Notes from last sync (Feb 6):
- SRE requested explicit checkbox for auto-fallback to ensure operators opt in
- Solutions Eng: prefer explicit confirmation copy that references rollback behavior and linking to support runbook
- Engineering: backend needs a deterministic API to report "isPinned" and fallback chain for UI to show in details page

Next steps (this doc owner):
- Build hi-fi modal in Figma and link new copy variants to components (action: Maya) — due Feb 24
- Create a short demo flow in staging to validate API for isPinned and fallback chain (action: Diego) — due Feb 21
- Create JIRA tasks for audit logs and telemetry events (action: Product Ops)

Raw ideas for future experiments (put into backlog):
- "Pin drift detection": email/report when pinned endpoints fall behind latest verified version by >3 releases
- "Auto-regen sample": when model updated, run a small eval on pinned endpoints and surface quality delta metrics to owner
- "Pin-by-snapshot": allow pinning to an evaluation snapshot (prompt set + model hash) rather than version string

Notes-to-self (quick):
- Keep copy concise in primary flow; users want minimal friction
- Save long explanations for documentation and tooltips, not the modal body
- Record every user action as telemetry event (create_endpoint, open_advanced, pin_version, confirm_pin)

End of draft.

Design artifacts and links will be attached in the Figma prototype once hi-fi is ready. For now, use the rough wireframe description above when building the initial prototype.
